open_points.subject: A07 mapped operation output disclosure class
open_points.text: A07 rule 3 says a binding output takes the class the binding declares “for the empty lists of a mapped operation over an empty list alike”; A13 rule 6 says “an empty list takes the highest class among the node's inputs”.
open_points.question: What disclosure class does an empty output list from a mapped operation node receive?
options: The binding output port's declared class
The highest class among the mapped node's inputs
open_points.default_guess: The binding output port's declared class

open_points.subject: A07 redaction of personal-data file lists
open_points.text: “The same holds for a `personal_data` file: an agent gets its digest and class, and not its size, media type or spool facts.”
open_points.question: For a `many` personal-data file value, does the agent receive one redacted entry per file, preserving count and order, or one redaction for the list as a whole; if the latter, what digest identifies the list?
options: An ordered list of each file's digest and class
One digest and class for the whole file list
A single opaque class marker with no file digests
open_points.default_guess: An ordered list of each file's digest and class

open_points.subject: A07 redacted failure-detail length
open_points.text: “A `failure_detail` whose class is above `open` ... is returned to an agent only as its length and that class.”
open_points.question: Is the disclosed length measured in Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or stored UTF-8 bytes after truncation?
options: Stored UTF-8 byte length after truncation
Unicode character count after truncation
Original UTF-8 byte length before truncation
open_points.default_guess: Stored UTF-8 byte length after truncation

open_points.subject: A17 credential value grammar and wire encoding
open_points.text: A credential file's content is “decoded as UTF-8” and refused when it “holds an empty value or a control character”, but the text does not define `control character` or how accepted non-ASCII text is encoded as an HTTP header value.
open_points.question: Which Unicode characters are valid in a credential value, what exactly counts as a control character, and how is an accepted non-ASCII value serialized on the wire?
options: Allow only printable ASCII and send those bytes
Reject Unicode Cc controls but send all other text as UTF-8 bytes
Use the HTTP client's supported header-value character repertoire
open_points.default_guess: Allow only printable ASCII and send those bytes

open_points.subject: A17 trailing newline removal
open_points.text: “its content decoded as UTF-8, without one trailing newline, is the value.”
open_points.question: Does one trailing newline mean one LF byte only, one CRLF sequence, either Unicode line ending, or all trailing newline sequences?
options: Remove exactly one trailing LF
Remove exactly one LF or CRLF sequence
Remove all trailing line-ending sequences

open_points.subject: A17 configuration-file protection on token reload
open_points.text: A17 says the configuration file “must be a regular file, not a symbolic link, owned by the kernel's user, with no permission for group or others; the kernel refuses to start otherwise”, while A16 says “Exactly four checks apply to a re-read” and lists only parsing and token checks.
open_points.question: When the token list is re-read after startup, must the kernel recheck the configuration file's regular-file, no-symlink, ownership and permission conditions, and what happens if only those attributes change while its bytes do not?
options: Recheck all A17 file protections on every request or re-read
Check those protections only at startup and apply only A16's four reload checks
Recheck protections only when the file bytes change
open_points.default_guess: Recheck all A17 file protections whenever the configuration file is opened

open_points.subject: A13 eligibility of an unmapped node
open_points.text: “a node is ready when every input port holds its value”; only the mapped-node clause says that a concluded element is never executed again and excludes elements that wait.
open_points.question: Is an unmapped node with a concluded NodeExecution or an active WaitingPoint excluded from `ready_nodes`, and exactly when does an approval, resolution or resume make a waiting node eligible again?
options: Exclude concluded nodes permanently and exclude waiting nodes until the current request releases their specific wait
Treat any node with all inputs as ready and let its operation rules suppress duplicate work
Exclude only concluded nodes; waiting nodes remain ready
open_points.default_guess: Exclude concluded nodes permanently and exclude waiting nodes until the current request releases their specific wait

open_points.subject: A13 meaning of a waiting element being executable
open_points.text: Rule 2 runs only a mapped element that “does not wait”, but rule 7 says “A waiting element can still execute”.
open_points.question: Does “can still execute” mean it is schedulable while its WaitingPoint exists, or only that it may become schedulable after a later approval, resolution or resume?
options: It may execute only after the relevant request removes or resolves its wait
It remains schedulable while waiting
Different waiting reasons have different eligibility
open_points.default_guess: It may execute only after the relevant request removes or resolves its wait

open_points.subject: A13 ordering of derived skip and upstream-failure records
open_points.text: A15 orders records for nodes “that become non-executable together” by (`node_id`, `map_index`), while A13 specifies the next executable node but does not place those derived records relative to execution of another ready independent node.
open_points.question: After a node concludes and causes skips or `upstream_failed` conclusions, are all newly forced records written before selecting the next ready executable node, after that node executes, or only when no executable nodes remain?
options: Write the full newly forced closure before selecting the next executable node
Select and execute the next ready node first
Defer forced records until no executable node remains
open_points.default_guess: Write the full newly forced closure before selecting the next executable node

open_points.subject: State 0 secret non-disclosure versus A17 transformed echoes
open_points.text: State 0 says credentials “never enter ... an answer”; A17 says a service response carrying a credential “in another encoding is not recognised, and is protected only by its class.”
open_points.question: Is the State 0 no-secret-in-an-answer guarantee limited to the credential's verbatim bytes, or must encoded or otherwise transformed credential values also be withheld?
options: Only verbatim credential bytes are detected and withheld
Recognized common encodings must also be detected and withheld
No service body derived from a credential may be returned
open_points.default_guess: Only verbatim credential bytes are detected and withheld, following the specific State 2 rule
